title: Assertion harness for partial-stream contract verification and graceful decoder fallback
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Build a focused assertion and test harness that verifies contracts emitted over streaming responses when JSON payloads are cut mid-token, and that validates graceful decoder fallback behavior (sanitizing sentinel, structured error payloads, or canonical partial assembly). The harness will simulate partial TCP chunks, interleaved tool call markers, and token-level noise. It aims to catch regressions in streaming parsers and constrained decoders across model variants and runtime kernel configurations.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can reproduce 6 canonical partial-stream failure modes (mid-string truncation, truncated number, cut key, extra trailing text, interleaved toolcall marker, kv-cache chunk boundary) and assert recovery policy outcomes.
When recovery policy == 'reconstruct', decoder reassembles partial fragments into a valid JSON object for 95% of non-malformed cases in CI smoke runs.
When recovery policy == 'fail-safe', model output is replaced by a stable sentinel payload that conforms to the schema (error_code + user_facing_message + partial_digest).

End-to-end test that includes an interleaved tool call: if tool returns before JSON completion, harness verifies tool-call envelope is preserved and JSON contract remains valid or falls back to sentinel according to policy.
Canary job runs on merge to main for runtime-1.22 and flags regressions when failure rate > 0.5% compared to baseline.
Clear runbook entries created for the two most common failure classes with remediation steps and log collection commands.
test_plan: Unit tests for decoder primitives (token-boundary detection, partial-merge heuristics, sentinel injection) with targeted fuzz vectors.
Integration harness that replays recorded model streams from production traces (anonymized) and injects simulated truncation at random offsets.
Cross-model matrix: run harness against curated model set (open-1.0, redwood-vX variants, and a quantized 4-bit variant) and collect metrics for pass/fail and fallback mode frequency.
Load-sensitivity test: run 100 parallel streaming sessions through the runtime to ensure batching/kv-cache interplay does not increase partial-emit rate above baseline.
CI job: nightly canary that posts results to the console dashboard and opens an alert issue when regression detected.
Manual QA: product partner reviews three representative failure traces and approves sentinel wording for UX clarity.
notes: Design trade-offs considered: aggressive reconstruction heuristics may mask underlying model instability; conservative sentinel-first approach is friendlier for downstream consumers but increases error surface.
We decided to implement a toggleable policy flag at the SDK level (reconstruct|sanitize|sentinel) so partners can choose behavior per route.
Performance budget: assertion checks should add <2% CPU overhead in streaming hot paths; heavier heuristics run in aux worker threads and report telemetry.
We will reuse the existing flight-recorder instrumentation from ENG-178530 to capture offsets and token boundaries for each streamed response.
If harness finds >1% divergence between quantized and float variants on structured contract pass rate, create follow-up to investigate kernel selection heuristics.
updates: 2026-03-03: Spike completed to reproduce mid-string truncation locally; initial heuristics implemented in decoder shim (Aisha).
2026-03-06: Reviewed approach with PM (Lina Chen) — agreed on sentinel schema and telemetry fields; added 'partial_digest' to sentinel for deterministic tracing.
2026-03-09: Integration harness successfully replayed 120 anonymized production streams and flagged 8 traces needing manual triage (only 2 were reconstruction candidates).
2026-03-12: Hooked canary job into nightly CI for runtime-1.22; initial baseline collected (pass rate 99.42% across curated models).
Next steps: finalize SDK flag surface, add roadmap item for SDK docs and examples, and prepare one-pager for customer-facing postmortem guidance.
